entities.summary: Philon, Athenian architect of the 4th century BC, is known as the planner of two important works: the portico of twelve Doric columns to the great Hall of the Mysteries at Eleusis and, under the administration of Lycurgus, an arsenal in Piraeus, Athens' port city. The arsenal was to hold the rigging of the galleys and was so contrived as to be 'perhaps known to us more in detail than any other lost monument of antiquity.' Philon's designs demonstrate his expertise in naval architecture, showcasing the strategic importance of Piraeus as a major maritime hub. The portico, built in 340 BCE, has been reconstructed and now stands as a testament to Philon's ingenuity and aesthetic vision. Philon's legacy extends beyond his architectural achievements, as he played a key role in shaping the development of Piraeus and its subsequent influence on the growth of Athens. The legacy of Philon's work can be seen in the modern city of Piraeus, which continues to serve as a major port and commercial center. Philon's innovative designs and leadership have left a lasting impact on the history of architecture and urban planning, cementing his place as one of the most important architects of the ancient world.
